tr.td: slow: the GPU holding the busiest experts sets the step.
TFLOP/s against the forced-even control run.
learns badly: a coefficient set too high makes the model learn worse, and one set too low leaves the load uneven.
LM loss and MaxVio together: with flat router probabilities, the aux loss can look balanced while the load stays uneven.

learns badly: balancing per sequence or per micro-batch keeps domain experts from forming. slow: balancing per global batch leaves the load on each GPU uneven; the step took 5.8% longer, mainly from that imbalance and about 1% of that slowdown from communication.
MaxVio at the scope you balance: per micro-batch or per global batch from the token counts, per sequence from the routing trace (A.1).
slow: with a fixed step of 1e-3, the busiest expert still gets about 20 times the mean load at 128 experts. learns badly: above 128 experts, that step is too coarse.
How far expert_bias spreads in each layer across checkpoints, and MaxVio per global batch from the token counts (A.1).
slow: smoothing the bias with a moving average makes it lag the router's scores. The bias is shared by the global batch, so each GPU's load can stay uneven, as in Scope.
MaxVio per micro-batch alongside MaxVio per global batch, from the saved token counts (A.1), to detect a globally balanced batch hiding local imbalance.
